about: Answers from the brand and legal team to the rulebook's open questions. lib/decisions.js applies each one in code and names it on the finding. A decided finding stays on the report as advisory; nothing is deleted. The rules themselves (brand_rules.json) are unchanged, so a decision can be reversed by deleting its entry.

decisions.question: Is 'acne' wording acceptable on a cosmetic in India? (open legal question Q1 in research/regulatory_sources.md)
decisions.scope: Acne wording: 'anti-acne', 'acne control', 'reduces acne', 'fights breakouts', 'clears breakouts', 'for acne-prone skin'. Still flagged: treat / cure / heal (drug claim, CLM-01, block), prevent / stop (the statute's own 'prevention' wording), elimination promises ('acne-free', 'no more acne', 'say goodbye to breakouts'), anti-bacterial claims, and every hair-fall claim, which the answer did not cover.
decisions.note: Acne wording accepted by brand/legal (DEC-01, 2026-10-04). Treat/cure, prevent/stop and 'acne-free' style promises are still flagged.

eval_relabels.why: The reviewer's only reason was open question Q1 ('arguably acne mitigation'), which DEC-01 answers.

decisions.question: Does Minimalist run comparison ('Us vs Them') ads?
decisions.scope: Keeps the Us vs Them format (template 17). It changes no rule: each comparison still needs like-for-like proof on file and its basis on the creative (CLM-12, ASCI Chapter IV), so comparison ads stay High risk and stay non-exportable until a reviewer attaches that proof.

decisions.question: Can the brand's taglines ('Hide Nothing.', 'Skin Science') appear on the creative?
decisions.scope: A judge finding whose whole quote is one of the taglines is kept for the record but not acted on. The taglines also need no citation as a tag (lib/brief_check.js).
decisions.note: Brand tagline: accepted by the brand team (DEC-03, 2026-10-04).

decisions.question: What risk level does an AI-made product texture (swatch beside the verified pack) carry?
decisions.scope: Texture shots made by ChatGPT from the label-verified pack: the pack is unchanged and checked word by word; only the swatch is AI. Risk Low; the small AI-generated - illustrative mark stays for transparency. AI people, hands, skin or result images stay Severe.

decisions.question: Can a pregnancy / lactation safety line that the product page itself states (e.g. "Pregnancy/Lactation: Safe") appear on an ad?
decisions.scope: Pregnancy and lactation safety wording as stated on the product listing. Baby / infant safety and age claims are not covered.
decisions.note: Pregnancy/lactation safety as stated on the listing accepted by the brand (DEC-06, 2026-10-05).

decisions.question: Should AI-made images (people, result frames, before/after, progress) block an ad?
decisions.answer: No. Make them, show a clear warning and keep the Severe risk rating.
decisions.scope: Every AI-01 finding: AI result images and AI people. The AI label is still drawn on every such image, and Severe-risk ads still need real, consented photos before export.
decisions.note: AI-made image: shown with a warning and rated Severe (DEC-07, 2026-10-05). India's ASCI rule on AI content (in force from about late December 2026) prohibits AI result images even with a label, so replace with real, consented photos before use.

policy_notes.question: Should claims that appear on the brand's own product listing be treated more leniently?
policy_notes.applied_in: lib/rules.js: listing-backed findings are lowered one step (PAGE_DENY is empty). A reviewer still confirms substantiation; the finding names the listing line.
